title: Log batch, v1 (server SDKs)
description: What a host server sends: POST /v1/logs {"lines": [<line>, …]} (at most 1000 lines and 4 MiB as sent; gzip with Content-Encoding: gzip, at most 32 MiB unpacked), Authorization: Bearer <server secret>. Each line stands alone: one that does not fit is refused and named, the rest go in. Scrub personal data before sending; the service scrubs again. A line's id is minted by the SDK, so sending a batch again is harmless.

id.description: Minted by the SDK (a ULID). A line whose id the project has already is not stored again.

at.description: When the host wrote it: ISO 8601 with microseconds and an offset. More than 5 minutes ahead of the service's clock: placed at now. Older than its environment keeps lines: refused.

message.description: Scrubbed. Over 32 KiB it is cut, not refused.

context.description: What the app passed along (Monolog's context), scrubbed, values under secret-looking keys removed. Over 64 KiB as JSON (with extra) it is replaced by a note.

extra.description: What the app's processors added (Monolog's extra), scrubbed.

environment.description: production, staging, local, … Lines are kept per project and environment.

release.description: The build this process runs (a git commit).

request_id.description: The same for every line of one HTTP request (and of the jobs it queued). An incoming X-Request-Id is kept when it fits. One that does not fit is left off; the line still goes in.

transaction.description: What was running, without values: "GET /properties/{property}", "job App\\Jobs\\SendInvoice", "artisan migrate".
